solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flounder and bass seen on Washington lake

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece seen on another follows it, so the bass part comes last

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake
a bass voice or note is low

explanation.surface: An angler reports catching a flatfish and a bass on a lake in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' and 'bass' both look like fish, but 'Flounder' is the verb and 'bass' means low.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to struggle clumsily, and to wallow is to roll about helplessly in mud or water, a near synonym.

clue.text: Smear with oil, developing tan around head?

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
a tan that is developing is still changing, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the head of an organisation is No. 1, written NO I

explanation.surface: A sunbather rubs on oil to deepen a tan, perhaps on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of an organisation is its No. 1, written NO I; the shuffled tan is split round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To anoint is to smear or rub with oil, especially in a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Public nuisance in US, 51, close to rehab, in gutter sadly

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: sadly says the gathered letters are in a sorry, jumbled state
the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A troubled American lies in the gutter, close to the rehab clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges LI, B and GUTTER together.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug, the American term, is someone who drops rubbish in public places, a public nuisance.

clue.text: Race by greedy woman to get discounted music player

parts.note: the Welsh are a people or race

indicators.note: discounted means something is knocked off, here the final letter of the word

parts.note: a harpy is a grasping, greedy woman

explanation.surface: A greedy woman cheats in a race to grab a cut-price music player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discounted' trims the last letter, Y, from HARPY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh harp is a triple-strung harp, an instrument someone plays, so a player of music.

clue.text: March about in religious ground I don't know

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the other piece

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, ground under religious authority

indicators.note: about means moving around, so the letters of March are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilgrim's march circles a holy site, and nobody knows why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month or a procession; a see is the area a bishop governs.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'search me' is a casual idiom admitting one has no idea.

clue.text: As discussed, observe deep fish

indicators.note: discussed means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to observe is to see
a bass voice is a deep one

explanation.surface: Someone recalls an earlier conversation about watching fish in deep water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As discussed' gives SEA for the sound of SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bass is a common edible marine fish.

clue.text: Financial backer raised support after seeing article

indicators.note: after seeing places the second piece below the first

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: An investor puts up money once a newspaper article has been read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LEG upwards to GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a private investor who backs a business or a theatre production.

clue.text: Resounding noise queen's ignored in error

indicators.note: ignored means left out of the word for error

parts.note: a clanger is a blunder or error
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A monarch's royal blunder is passed over amid the din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen's ignored' reads as 'the queen is ignored'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic sound.

clue.text: Scotsman on-air chewed Italian food

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters of on-air are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish broadcaster eats pasta live on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges ONAIR to ARONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a tubular pasta, a staple Italian food.

clue.text: Manuel's dish? Everyone has it with tripe that's passed round

indicators.note: passed round suggests turning the whole string about, reading it backwards

parts.note: all means everyone
tripe is nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: Manuel, the Spanish waiter from Fawlty Towers, serves a tripe dish to the whole table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed round' reads ALLITROT backwards. Manuel is the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, so his dish is a Spanish one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a Spanish omelette, a dish a Spaniard like Manuel might serve.

clue.text: Cricket shot, cut clinically by Glamorgan's opener

indicators.note: by puts the next piece beside the first
an opener comes first, so only the initial letter is used

parts.note: to lance is to cut with a surgeon's lancet

explanation.surface: Glamorgan's opening batsman plays a crisp, clinical cut shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan is a Welsh county cricket club, and 'opener' is also a cricketing term, so the surface hides the letter pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a cricket stroke deflecting the ball fine off the bat's face.

clue.text: Involve outsiders to explain chaos reported by drunkard?

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters
a drunkard slurs, so the spoken word comes out with a different hiss

parts.note: chaos is a mess

explanation.surface: Someone tries to involve outsiders to explain the chaos a drunkard described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported by drunkard?' turns MESS into the slurred MESH.
explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to entangle someone, to involve them in something difficult.

clue.text: Friend absorbs for example soldier's symbolic narration

indicators.note: absorbs means takes inside, so the friend word surrounds the others

parts.note: an ally is a friend
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A friend takes in a soldier's war story, told in symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, 'other ranks', is the usual crossword soldier; the 's links soldier to the narration in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events symbolise a deeper meaning.

clue.text: Bird getting divorce from you finally

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A woman finally gets her divorce, a 'bird' in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Stand up vintage miniature to face speculators

indicators.note: to face places these pieces after the speculators, facing them

parts.note: bears are stock-market speculators betting on a fall
cru is a wine term for a vintage or growth
tiny means miniature

explanation.surface: Someone stands up a miniature bottle of vintage wine for investors to inspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand up' looks like an instruction but is the definition of a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear scrutiny is to stand up to close examination.

clue.text: Author, seeing learner in street, had turned left

indicators.note: in puts the learner letter inside the street word

parts.note: a road is a street
L is a learner, from the British L-plate

indicators.note: turned means the word had is read backwards

explanation.surface: A learner driver in the street turns left on seeing a famous writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives DAH from HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl was a British writer of children's books such as Matilda.

clue.text: Study philosopher? After time, it's routine drudgery

indicators.note: after places these pieces below the time letter

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
John Stuart Mill was a philosopher

explanation.surface: Studying philosophy, after a while, becomes a dull grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read' is the British term for studying a subject at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill, literally a mill turned by walking, is figuratively any monotonous routine.

clue.text: My French pseudonym used, when exchanging painting

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: exchanging means two letters of the pseudonym swap places

parts.note: an alias is a pseudonym in use

explanation.surface: A French artist signs a painting under a pseudonym when selling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging' swaps the last two letters of ALIAS, giving ALISA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa is Leonardo da Vinci's famous portrait painting in the Louvre.

clue.text: Wise man following group has weathered stormy sea voyage

indicators.note: following places the wise man after the rearranged letters
weathered means worn into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise man trails a group that has come through a storm at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weathered' rearranges GROUPHAS to ROUGHPAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough passage is a sea crossing in heavy weather, literally a stormy voyage.

clue.text: Fell when briefly jogging

indicators.note: jogging means jolted about, so the letters are rearranged
briefly means cut short, losing the end of the word

explanation.surface: A runner fell over while out jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts WHEN to WHE, then 'jogging' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree is to cut it down, as to hew is to chop with an axe.

clue.text: Country girl beneath river losing heart

indicators.note: in a down answer, beneath places the girl below the river
losing heart means the middle letter of the river drops out

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris
gal is a girl

explanation.surface: A country girl lives below a river and is losing heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' takes I from the middle of SEINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: US city centres to sell alpaca? True

indicators.note: the centres of the two words are their middle letters

parts.note: so means true, as in 'that is so'

explanation.surface: A trader in an American city sells alpaca wool, really.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a city in Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Tired vehicle owner crashed

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: crashed means smashed up, so the letters of owner are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exhausted motorist has crashed the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges OWNER to EWORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Careworn means worn out and weary from worry.

clue.text: Discharge emptied underground enters English river

indicators.note: enters means goes inside the river word

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, leaving only the ends

explanation.surface: An outflow from an underground drain runs into an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' reduces UNDERGROUND to UD, which 'enters' EXE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude is to discharge or ooze out slowly.

clue.text: Speak in public for a test, partly

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone must give a speech in public as a kind of test.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, to address an audience.

clue.text: Hanging around day after day, jobseekers receive this piece of cake

indicators.note: hanging around something is surrounding it, so the jobseekers word encloses the days

parts.note: the dole is unemployment benefit paid to jobseekers

indicators.note: after joins one day letter to the other

explanation.surface: Day after day, the unemployed hang about and are given a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dole' is British for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddle is British slang for a very easy task, like a piece of cake.

clue.text: Bon e to lie next to another that is nameless

indicators.note: next to places the two pieces side by side

parts.note: to fib is to tell a small lie

indicators.note: nameless means losing N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: the ulna is another bone of the arm, beside the radius

explanation.surface: One bone lies next to another bone that has no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to the definition: another bone, the ULNA, which drops N for name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibula is the outer, thinner bone of the lower leg.

clue.text: Importance one attached to reducing sauce, tasted halfway through

indicators.note: attached to places the numeral after the cut sauce
reducing means cut down, losing its last letter

parts.note: gravy is a meat sauce
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: halfway through means only the first half of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A cook reducing a sauce adds one more ingredient, tasting as she goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reducing' cuts GRAVY to GRAV; 'halfway through' gives TAS, the first half of TASTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas means seriousness and weight, giving someone importance and dignity.

clue.text: Flowering plant's on stand in lobby

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the lobby word

parts.note: a hall is an entrance lobby
re means on, concerning
to let something be is to let it stand

explanation.surface: A potted flowering plant sits on a stand in the hotel lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means RE, 'about', not position; 'stand' as BE is the sense of 'let it be'.
explanation.definitionFit: The harebell is a wild flowering plant with pale blue bell-shaped flowers.

clue.text: One quietly avoids ice-cream in lounge

indicators.note: avoids means leaves out the letters that follow

parts.note: a lollipop, an ice lolly, is a frozen treat on a stick
I is the Roman numeral one
p, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone quietly turns down an ice-cream in the lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' removes I and P from LOLLIPOP. 'lounge' looks like a room but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to lounge or loll about lazily, as well as to bound clumsily.
